arxiv-1601-01738.title: Spectral projected gradient method for generalized tensor eigenvalue complementarity problem
arxiv-1601-01738.creator: Gaohang Yu, Yisheng Song, Yi Xu, Zefeng Yu
arxiv-1601-01738.description: Abstract This paper looks at the tensor eigenvalue complementarity problem (TEiCP) which arises from the stability analysis of finite dimensional mechanical systems and is closely related to the optimality conditions for polynomial optimization. We investigate two monotone ascent spectral projected gradient (SPG) methods for TEiCP.

arxiv-2106-10823.title: 3D Object Detection for Autonomous Driving: A Survey
arxiv-2106-10823.creator: Rui Qian, Xin Lai, Xirong Li
arxiv-2106-10823.description: Abstract Autonomous driving is regarded as one of the most promising remedies to shield human beings from severe crashes. To this end, 3D object detection serves as the core basis of perception stack especially for the sake of path planning, motion prediction, and collision avoidance etc \xspace .

arxiv-2206-05376.title: A Distorted Charged Dilaton Black Ring
arxiv-2206-05376.creator: Shohreh Abdolrahimi a,b and Christos C. Tzounis a,c
arxiv-2206-05376.description: Abstract We present the distorted five dimensional static black rings in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton (EMd) gravity by using the sigma model structure of the dimensionally reduced field equations. We investigate how a static and neutral distribution of external matter distorts the black ring.

arxiv-2210-06992.title: S 4 S_{4} -quartics with Prescribed Norms
arxiv-2210-06992.creator: Sebastian Monnet
arxiv-2210-06992.description: Abstract . Given a number field k k and a finitely generated subgroup 𝒜 ⊆ k ∗ \mathcal{A}\subseteq k^{*} , we study the distribution of S 4 S_{4} -quartic extensions of k k such that the elements of 𝒜 \mathcal{A} are norms.

arxiv-2401-06444.title: Strategies for the Integration of quantum networks for a future quantum internet
arxiv-2401-06444.creator: M.I. García-Cid, L. Ortiz, J. Sáez, V. Martín
arxiv-2401-06444.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by M.I. García-Cid, L. Ortiz, J. Sáez, V. Martín. The great scientific and technological advances that are being carried out in the field of quantum communications, accompanied by large investment programs such as EuroQCI, are driving the deployment of quantum network throughout the world. One of the final long-term objectives is to achieve the development of a quantum internet that provides greater security in its services and new functionalities that the current internet does not have.

arxiv-2402-02072.title: Searching for singlet vector-like leptons via pair production at ILC
arxiv-2402-02072.creator: Chong-Xing Yue 1,2, Yue-Qi Wang 1,2, Han Wang 1,2, Yi-Hang Wang 1,2, Si Li 1,2
arxiv-2402-02072.description: Abstract Vector-like leptons (VLLs) as one kind of the most intriguing particles, have been widely concerned in several extensions of the Standard Model (SM). In this work, we explore the discovery potential of VLLs via pair production in the context of models that satisfy asymptotic safety at the International Linear Collider (ILC).

arxiv-2404-00115.title: On polynomial solutions to the minimal surface equation
arxiv-2404-00115.creator: Yifan Guo
arxiv-2404-00115.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yifan Guo. We are interested in finding nonlinear polynomials P P on ℝ n \mathbb{R}^{n} that solves the minimal surface equation. We first prove a structure theorem on such polynomials. We show that the highest degree term P m P_{m} must factor as P 0 k ​ Q m P_{0}^{k}Q_{m} where k k is odd, Q m ≥ 0 Q_{m}\geq 0 on ℝ n \mathbb{R}^{n} and P 0 P_{0} is irreducible, and that the level sets of P m P_{m} are all area minimizing.

pmc-10520345.title: A cysteine protease inhibitor GC376 displays potent antiviral activity against coxsackievirus infection
pmc-10520345.creator: Yongkang Chen, Xiaohong Li, Min Wang, Yuan Li, Jun Fan, Jingjing Yan, Shuye Zhang, Lu Lu, Peng Zou
pmc-10520345.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Highlights•GC376 inhibits coxsackievirus infection and reduces the yield of progeny virions.•GC376 suppresses viral RNA replication by blocking the activity of viral 3C protease.•GC376 exhibited antiviral activity against various serotypes of coxsackieviruses.Keywords: Coxsackievirus, Cysteine protease, 3C protease, Protease inhibitor, Antiviral, GC376

Introduction

Coxsackievirus is one of the non-enveloped RNA viruses, and its infection can cause hand-foot-mouth disease (HFMD), posing a serious threat to the health of children worldwide, especially those less than 5 years old (Chen et al., 2017; Guo et al., 2022).

pmc-11415040.title: Comparison of routine del Nido cardioplegia vs two types of modified del Nido cardioplegias for myocardial protection among patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) surgeries: A randomized double-blind clinical trial
pmc-11415040.creator: Babar Ali, Salman Pervaiz Butt, Mohammad Ghazi Nour, Mohammad Bagher Khosravi, Naeimehossadat Asmarian, Ali Raza Shoul, Arun Kumar, Umer Darr, Gopal Bhatnagar
pmc-11415040.description: Background: The del Nido cardioplegia solution is a widely used method for myocardial protection in various settings. However, there is limited evidence of its effectiveness in adult cardiac surgery, and the baseline solution, Plasma Lyte A, is not readily available, leading to the use of alternative baseline solutions.

pmc-11462745.title: Real-world evidence study on the impact of SPECT MPI, PET MPI, cCTA and stress echocardiography on downstream healthcare utilisation in patients with coronary artery disease in the US
pmc-11462745.creator: Matthieu Pelletier-Galarneau, Arturo Cabra, Erika Szabo, Santosh Angadageri
pmc-11462745.description: BackgroundCoronary artery disease (CAD) is associated with a large clinical and economic burden. However, consensus on the optimal approach to CAD diagnosis is lacking. This study sought to compare downstream healthcare resource utilisation following different cardiac imaging modalities, to inform test selection for CAD diagnosis.

pmc-12495263.title: Transforming Pediatric Physiotherapy: The Role of ChatGPT in Therapy, Limitations, and Ethical Considerations
pmc-12495263.creator: Hussein M Ziab, Rami Mazbouh, Fatima Siblini, Abdulqadir J Nashwan
pmc-12495263.description: The use of large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT in pediatric physiotherapy, is a big step forward in the provision of tailored care, clinical decision-making, and caregiver education. This narrative review examines ChatGPT's roles in improving physiotherapy practice across three major domains: (1) clinical reasoning, (2) tailored therapeutic recommendations, and (3) caregiver engagement.

pmc-12607428.title: From Science to Innovation in Aquatic Animal Nutrition: A Global TRL-Based Assessment of Insect-Derived Feed Technologies via Scientific Publications and Patents
pmc-12607428.creator: Cristina M Quintella, Grace Ferreira Ghesti, Ricardo Salgado, Ana M A T Mata, Sofia Engrola
pmc-12607428.description: Simple SummaryAquaculture plays a critical role in feeding the world but usually requires feed from unsustainable sources like wild fish leftovers. Insects are an alternative because they are nutritious, grow fast, and can be raised on organic waste, turning problems into resources and supporting the circular economy. This study explored how insect-based feeds are being developed and shared worldwide.

pmc-12617829.title: Mobile Apps for HIV and Sexually Transmitted Infection Prevention in Canada, Mexico, and the United States: Environmental Scan
pmc-12617829.creator: Higinio Fernández-Sánchez, Javier Salazar-Alberto, Jhan Carlos Manuel Fernández-Delgado, Annalynn Galvin, Michael J Mugavero, Carlos E Rodriguez-Diaz, Diane Santa Maria, Lorraine Buis
pmc-12617829.description: BackgroundCanada, Mexico, and the United States are primary transit destinations for migrants in the Western Hemisphere. Migrants face barriers to accessing health services, including HIV and AIDS and sexually transmitted infection (STI) prevention. Mobile apps may enhance public health access for these populations.

pmc-13072603.title: Self-esteem patterns and the associations with health-related quality of life, self-rated health and lifestyle behaviour among junior high school students: a latent class analysis
pmc-13072603.creator: Ruowei Wang, Shuna Zhai, Chunhong Shen, Jiaoyang Liu, Pei Zhang, Tong Zhang, Qingai Yang, Xiangzheng Ding, Aihua Wang, Xiuyun Wu
pmc-13072603.description: BackgroundPrevious studies have investigated associations of self-esteem with mental health among adolescents. Very few studies have examined the relationship of self-esteem patterns with health-related quality of life (HRQoL), mental health and lifestyle behaviour. This study aims to explore patterns of self-esteem, and analyze their associations with HRQoL, self-rated health, mental health and lifestyle behaviour among junior high school students.

pmc-13266132.title: Bundibugyo Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda: A PHEIC in a countermeasure gap
pmc-13266132.creator: Mohamed Abdirahim Omar, Ahmed Abdinasir Abdule
pmc-13266132.description: rmined that Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus in the DRC and Uganda met PHEIC criteria under the International Health Regulations. As of May 15, 2026, WHO reported 246 suspected cases and 80 deaths in affected health zones in Ituri Province, DRC, with laboratory-confirmed imported cases reported in Uganda [1].

pmc-13381424.title: Identification of prognostic genes and development of a risk model for pancreatic cancer based on hypoxia- and lipid metabolism-related genes
pmc-13381424.creator: Xiangshu Guo, Jianqi Xiong, Longxing Niu, Shaolin Li
pmc-13381424.description: BackgroundPancreatic cancer (PC) is associated with a poor prognosis and limited therapeutic options because most patients are diagnosed at an advanced stage. Hypoxia- and lipid metabolism-related genes (HLPGs) play important roles in cancer progression. This study aimed to identify HLPGs-based prognostic genes in PC and explore their potential mechanisms, thereby providing a scientific basis for clinical management.

pmc-13535119.title: A Rare Case of Cutaneous Metastasis From Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma (OSCC) and the Possible Role of GALR2 as a Biomarker: A Case Report
pmc-13535119.creator: Ianny Brum Reis, Milena Moraes de Carvalho, Danilo Paschoal Ferrarezi, Natalie Aparecida Rodrigues Fernandes, Camyla Rodrigues Nascimento, Álvaro Formoso Pelegrini, Aldenora Maria Ximenes Rodrigues, Alex de Freitas Porsani, Flávio Ferlin Arbex, Carlos Rossa Junior
pmc-13535119.description: We report a rare case of cutaneous metastasis from oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). The primary tumor showed low expression of Galanin, CD68, GALR2, and Collagen IV, with increased FOXP3 and Vimentin. Systemic analysis revealed reduced CD8+ cells and increased Tregs. The patient died following aggressive disease progression.
